strategy.observation: Transistor serves over 30,000 podcasts and says its customers include small businesses and enterprise companies.
strategy.offer_link: If Transistor is already the host for a large base of B2B-oriented shows, a partnership with a production service could give some of those customers a way to outsource editing and show notes after they choose hosting.
hypotheses: Many Transistor customers may need help turning recordings into publish-ready episodes.
The partnerships team may be open to referring or bundling non-technical services for customers.
B2B brands using Transistor may value an external team for recurring editing and show notes.
Transistor may consider service partners that complement hosting and distribution rather than compete with them.
strategy.angle: With 30,000+ podcasts on Transistor, I wanted to see whether you ever partner with outside teams that handle editing and show notes for B2B shows.
strategy.fit_reason: The fit is plausible because Transistor has a large podcast customer base and a partnerships lead could manage service relationships, but the facts do not show an existing partner marketplace or a stated need for production services, so the link is a stretch.

draft.subject: Podcast production partners
draft.body:
Hi,

With 30,000+ podcasts on Transistor, I wanted to see whether you ever partner with outside teams that handle editing and show notes for B2B shows.

I help B2B brands turn recordings into publish-ready episodes, which can take some of the recurring production work off their team. If Transistor customers are asking for that kind of support, it could sit nicely alongside hosting.

Do you currently refer production help like that, or is it handled case by case?
